1  COMPENSATION AND TRANSPARENCY IN LAND ACQUISITION,
 REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT ACT, 2013, AGAINST THE  JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 23.03.2021 PASSED IN  LAC.NO.476/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL DISTRICT AND  SESSIONS JUDGE, BELAGAVI, DISMISSING THE REFERENCE  PETITION FILED UNDER SECTION 64 OF RIGHT TO FAIR  COMPENSATION AND TRANSPARENCY IN LAND ACQUISITION,
 REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT ACT, 2013.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:12437  MFA No. 100114 of 2022  JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the land-loser.

The appellant claimed higher compensation in LAC No.476/2017 on the file of the I Additional District Judge, Belagavi by filing a reference petition,
disputing the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
2. The Reference Court held that the petition is in time.

However, the Reference Court has confirmed the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer on the premise that the claimant has not led any evidence in support of his claim seeking enhancement.
3. This Court has perused the impugned judgment and award.
4. Except observing that petitioner has not led evidence, the Reference Court has not assigned any reasons as to why it is confirming the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
It is also brought to the notice of this Court that on 23.03.2021, the claimant was not present before the Reference Court when the case was listed for evidence of the claimant.
Since the claimant was not present, the Court held that there is no evidence on behalf of claimant and passed the impugned award.
In the month of March 2021, there were restrictions on movements due to Covid-19 pandemic.
Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that this Court in similar circumstances in MFA 100018/2022 has allowed the appeal and remanded the matter for fresh consideration.
6. Learned counsel for the respondents, Sri. Umesh Ainapur does not dispute the fact that in a similar case, this Court has allowed the appeal and remanded the matter for fresh consideration.

However, Sri. Umesh Ainapur submits that Reference Court is justified in confirming the award of the Special Land Acquisition Officer, when there was no evidence led in by the appellant to justify Dundappa Rudragouda Biradar vs The Special Land Acquistion Officer on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103721241/
2 his claim for enhancement.
7.

sentences.text: This Court is of the view that the impugned order is not a speaking order.
It is well settled principle of law that when the Reference Court has to assign the reasons while dismissing or allowing the reference petition.
Even if no evidence is led, the Court has to assess the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer based on the materials considered by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
The Court is under obligation to satisfy itself that the market value is determined by taking into consideration all the relevant factors.
The said exercise is not carried out.
Moreover, in March 2021, when the case was posted for claimant's evidence, there were few restrictions on the movement due to Covid -19 pandemic.
The Reference Court could not have dismissed the petition on the premise that the petitioner before it was not present to lead evidence.
9. For the reasons assigned above, the impugned judgment and award are to be set aside.

Hence, the following:
ORDER 1.
Appeal is allowed in part.
2. The impugned Judgment and award dated 23.03.2021 are set aside.
The matter is remanded to the Reference Court to consider and pass the award in accordance with law.
3. It is further made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the matter.
4. All contentions of the parties, except plea of limitation, which is already decided in favour of the appellant, are kept open.
Parties shall appear before the reference Court on 09.11.2023 without waiting for any further notice from the reference Court.
